animation.layers.desc: Layer-shell surfaces appearing, mapping, closing, moving, resizing, or taking and losing the keyboard

appearance.blur.optimized.desc: Share one cached background blur across surfaces on an output.

appearance.border_width.desc: Inner border width in logical pixels.

appearance.corner_radius.desc: Radius of the complete decorated window.

appearance.opaque_fullscreen.desc: Draw fullscreen windows over the backdrop and ignore window rule `opacity`.

appearance.outer_border_width.desc: Outer ring width in logical pixels.

appearance.shadow.enabled.desc: Draw shadows behind tiled and floating windows.

appearance.tab_bar.font.desc: Title font as a Pango description, such as `"Inter Bold 9"`.

appearance.tab_bar.height.desc: Thickness in logical pixels, from 2 to 400: the bar's height on the top or bottom, its width on the left or right. The group reserves the bar and one `gap` beside it. Give a side bar with titles room for them, such as `160`.

appearance.tab_bar.hide_when_single.desc: Draw no bar, and reserve no space, while a tab group holds one window. It stays a group, so the next window to join becomes a tab.

appearance.tab_bar.max_tabs.desc: Slots the bar shows at once, from 0 to 64; `0` shows every tab.

appearance.tab_bar.overflow.desc: What a bar does with more tabs than `max_tabs`. `"scroll"` keeps the slots at their size and shows a run of tabs that follows the active one, with a `‹` and a `›` button at the ends that select the previous and next tab. `"shrink"` narrows the slots until every tab fits.

appearance.tab_bar.padding.desc: Space a title keeps from either end of its slot.

appearance.tab_bar.position.desc: The group edge the bar sits on: `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, or `"right"`. On the top or bottom the slots sit side by side; on the left or right they stack, a vertical tab list whose titles still read across.

appearance.tab_bar.style.desc: `"titles"` shows each tab's title in its slot. `"indicator"` draws the slots alone; pair it with a small `height` for a thin strip.

appearance.tab_bar.title_format.desc: Slot label. `{title}`, `{app_id}`, and `{index}` (from 1) are replaced; a window without a title shows its app id.

appearance.tab_bar.visible.desc: Draw bars. `false` hides the bar of every group that has not shown its own with `column-show-tab-bar` or `column-toggle-tab-bar`; the tabs take its space and keep working from the keyboard. Those actions hide or show one group's bar whatever this says.

colors.accent_primary.desc: Titles, key chords, and primary emphasis.

colors.backdrop.desc: Fullscreen background and RGB color of the opaque emergency lock blank.

colors.background.desc: Background for Umbriel panels and banners.

colors.overview.background_tint.desc: Tint over the desktop behind the overview.

colors.tab_bar.active.desc: The active tab's slot in the focused column.

colors.tab_bar.active_unfocused.desc: The active tab's slot in any other column.

colors.tab_bar.background.desc: Slots of tabs that are neither active nor urgent.

colors.tab_bar.urgent.desc: The slot of a hidden tab that asks for attention.

drm.ignored_devices.desc: Absolute card or render-node paths. Prefer stable `/dev/dri/by-path` links.

effects.border.desc: Border preset or pool for the focused window.

effects.cursor.desc: Cursor preset or pool, shared across outputs.

effects.in_capture.desc: Include window, screen, and cursor effects in screencopy and image-copy captures. Border effects always appear, and an export-dmabuf capture always sees the same frame as the display, regardless of this setting.

effects.max_fps.desc: Cap, 0 to 240, for frames drawn only because an effect animates. `0` follows each output's refresh rate.

effects.pool.<name>.choose.desc: Ordered names of presets of that kind.

effects.preset.<name>.light.spread.desc: How far light from the ring spills, 1 to 256 logical pixels. Defining `[effects.preset.<name>.light]` enables light.

effects.preset.<name>.light.threshold.desc: Brightness a ring pixel needs before it emits, 0 to 1.

effects.preset.<name>.overlay.desc: A window preset drawn on the window while the border effect applies.

effects.preset.<name>.palette.desc: Supply `[colors]` accent and status colors to the program.

effects.preset.<name>.shader.desc: Path to the GLSL source, at most 256 KiB. Without it the preset is inert.

effects.preset.<name>.speed.desc: Multiplier on `umbriel_time`, 0 to 10. `0` holds `umbriel_time` at zero.

effects.screen.desc: Screen preset or pool applied to every output.

effects.window.desc: Window preset or pool applied to every window.

general.autostart.desc: Commands started once with the session. Changes require a restart.

general.focus_on_activate.desc: Let application activation requests focus and reveal their target.

general.honor_restored_maximize.desc: Honor maximize requests an application makes while its window opens, until it acknowledges its opening layout.

general.show_cheatsheet.desc: Show the keybind cheatsheet when Umbriel starts.

general.xwayland.desc: Start Xwayland lazily for X11 applications. Changes require a restart.

general.xwayland_native_resolution.desc: Show outputs to X11 applications at their physical resolution, so they render sharp on scaled outputs. Changes require a restart.

general.xwayland_xsettings.desc: Announce the interface scale and cursor theme to X11 applications through XSETTINGS. Turn it off to run your own XSETTINGS manager, such as `xsettingsd`. Changes require a restart.

hot_corners.bottom_left.action.desc: Any action accepted by a keybind.

hot_corners.bottom_right.action.desc: Any action accepted by a keybind.

hot_corners.top_left.action.desc: Any action accepted by a keybind.

hot_corners.top_right.action.desc: Any action accepted by a keybind.

input.cursor.hardware_cursor.desc: Use a hardware cursor plane when available.

input.cursor.hide_timeout_ms.desc: Hide after inactivity; `0` disables the timeout.

input.cursor.hide_when_typing.desc: Hide after a non-modifier key press.

input.cursor.theme.desc: Xcursor theme; empty uses the environment default.

input.device[].accel_profile.desc: Use `"flat"`, `"adaptive"`, or a custom acceleration curve.

input.device[].disable_while_typing.desc: Disable the touchpad during keyboard input.

input.device[].left_handed.desc: Swap the primary and secondary buttons.

input.device[].natural_scroll.desc: Reverse scrolling and three-finger gesture direction.

input.device[].repeat_delay.desc: Delay before a held key repeats.

input.device[].repeat_rate.desc: Key repeats per second; `0` disables repeat.

input.device[].tap_button_map.desc: Buttons for one-, two-, and three-finger taps: `"left_right_middle"` or `"left_middle_right"`.

input.drag_edge_scroll.delay_ms.desc: Time inside the zone before scrolling starts.

input.drag_edge_scroll.enabled.desc: Enable edge scrolling during a data drag or a tiled window move.

input.drag_edge_scroll.max_speed.desc: Peak scroll speed in logical pixels per second.

input.drag_edge_scroll.trigger_zone.desc: Width of the zone at each end, in logical pixels.

input.keyboard.numlock_toggle.desc: Enable NumLock when a keyboard connects.

input.keyboard.repeat_delay.desc: Delay before a held key repeats.

input.keyboard.repeat_rate.desc: Key repeats per second; `0` disables repeat.

input.keyboard.track_layout.desc: Choose session-wide or per-window layout tracking.

input.mouse.accel_profile.desc: Use `"flat"`, `"adaptive"`, or a custom acceleration curve.

input.mouse.left_handed.desc: Swap the primary and secondary buttons.

input.mouse.natural_scroll.desc: Reverse scrolling and three-finger gesture direction.

input.tablet.calibration_matrix.desc: Pass a six-number calibration matrix to libinput.

input.tablet.map_to_focused_output.desc: Follow the output holding keyboard focus.

input.tablet.map_to_focused_window.desc: Map the tablet area to the focused window.

input.tablet.map_to_output.desc: Confine the tablet to a connector or monitor name.

input.touch.map_to_output.desc: Confine touch input to a connector or monitor name.

input.touchpad.accel_profile.desc: Use `"flat"`, `"adaptive"`, or a custom acceleration curve.

input.touchpad.disable_on_external_mouse.desc: Disable the touchpad while an external mouse is connected.

input.touchpad.disable_while_typing.desc: Disable the touchpad during keyboard input.

input.touchpad.left_handed.desc: Swap the primary and secondary buttons.

input.touchpad.natural_scroll.desc: Reverse scrolling and three-finger gesture direction.

input.touchpad.scroll_factor.horizontal.desc: Lanes run top to bottom; windows sit left to right.

input.touchpad.scroll_factor.vertical.desc: Columns run left to right; windows stack top to bottom.

input.touchpad.tap_button_map.desc: Buttons for one-, two-, and three-finger taps: `"left_right_middle"` or `"left_middle_right"`.

layer_rule[].blur.desc: Enable/disable blur for the layer surface.

layer_rule[].blur_ignore_alpha.desc: Skip blur below an alpha threshold.

layer_rule[].blur_popups.desc: Enable/disable blur for descendant XDG popups.

layer_rule[].match.at_startup.desc: Match during or after the first 60 seconds.

layout.client_maximize.desc: What a tiled window's own maximize button does: `"column"` fills the column like `window-toggle-maximize`, `"edges"` fills the usable area without struts, gaps, or borders like `window-toggle-maximize-to-edges`. See Maximize and fullscreen.

layout.dwindle.new_toward_cursor.desc: Place a new window on the half of the focused tile nearer the pointer.

layout.dwindle.preserve_split.desc: Keep each split direction fixed after creation.

layout.extent_presets.desc: Fractions used by primary and secondary extent cycle actions, in any order; cycling steps by size.

layout.gap.desc: Gap between windows in logical pixels.

layout.master.new_becomes_master.desc: Give the master slot to each new window.

layout.master.new_on_top.desc: Put new stack windows at the top.

layout.new_exits_fullscreen.desc: Kinds of arriving window that make a fullscreen window on the workspace leave fullscreen. See Leaving fullscreen.

layout.scrolling.center_focused.desc: Use `"never"`, `"always"`, or `"on_overflow"` to control focus centering.

layout.scrolling.center_underfull_strip.desc: Center a strip narrower than the viewport.

layout.scrolling.default_extent_fraction.desc: Initial column extent from 0.1 to 1.0. The packaged config uses `0.5`.

layout.tabs.default_display.desc: How new columns and master areas show their windows: `"normal"`, or `"tabbed"` to start each as a tab group.

layout.tabs.middle_click_closes.desc: Close a tab with a middle click on its slot.

layout.tabs.new_tab_position.desc: Where a consumed, pulled, or dropped window joins a tab group: `"end"`, or `"after_active"` beside the active tab.

layout.tabs.scroll_switches_tabs.desc: Step through tabs with the wheel over the bar.

output.<name>.bit_depth.desc: Render bit depth for SDR output: `8` or `10`.

output.<name>.cyclic_workspaces.desc: Wrap a workspace step around the ends of the inventory.

output.<name>.direct_scanout.desc: Allow eligible fullscreen buffers to bypass composition.

output.<name>.enabled.desc: Turn the monitor on or off.

output.<name>.focus_at_startup.desc: Move the mouse cursor to this monitor on startup.

output.<name>.layout.scrolling.default_e.desc: Initial scrolling-column extent on this output.

output.<name>.min_workspaces.desc: Minimum count for a dynamic output.

output.<name>.mode.desc: Resolution and optional refresh rate, such as `"2560x1440@165"`.

output.<name>.screen_effect.desc: Replace `effects.screen` with a screen preset or pool, or `"off"` to disable it on this output.

output.<name>.sdr_transfer.desc: Transfer curve for untagged SDR on HDR outputs: `"gamma22"` or `"srgb"`.

output.<name>.sdr_white.desc: SDR reference white in cd/m² while HDR is active.

output.<name>.tearing.desc: Allow eligible fullscreen windows to use asynchronous page flips.

overview.background_blur.desc: Blur the desktop behind the overview.

overview.shortcuts.desc: Show and accept keyboard shortcut badges.

overview.workspace_wallpaper.desc: Show each output's background inside its workspace previews.

screencast.desc: Manual target and focus-following screencast commands

screencast.disable_dynamic_confirmation.desc: Apply set and follow actions immediately without first confirming them. This can expose another window or output after an accidental key press.

security_context_rule[].match.app_id.desc: Exact regular-expression match against the application ID.

security_context_rule[].match.sandbox_en.desc: Exact regular-expression match against the sandbox engine.

window_rule[].background_render.desc: Keep this window drawing while hidden (default `false`). See Background rendering.

window_rule[].blur_ignore_alpha.desc: Skip blur below an alpha threshold.

window_rule[].blur_popups.desc: Apply blur to descendant XDG popups.

window_rule[].border_effect.desc: Replace `effects.border` with a border preset or pool, or `"off"` to disable it.

window_rule[].confine_pointer.desc: Keep the pointer inside this window while it has keyboard focus (default `false`).

window_rule[].default_column_display.desc: Show the column the window opens in as `"tabbed"` or `"normal"`.

window_rule[].default_floating_size.desc: Fraction of the output usable area.

window_rule[].default_floating_size_px.desc: Logical-pixel size, such as `{ width = 800, height = 600 }`.

window_rule[].default_focused.desc: Choose whether the new window takes focus.

window_rule[].default_maximize.desc: Open maximized within normal layout bounds.

window_rule[].default_maximize_to_edges.desc: Open maximized without gaps, struts, or borders.

window_rule[].default_output.desc: Open on a connector or monitor name.

window_rule[].default_scratchpad.desc: Store in the implicit or a configured scratchpad.

window_rule[].default_scrolling_column.desc: Join matching windows into one named scrolling column.

window_rule[].default_scrolling_column_o.desc: Set order inside a named scrolling column.

window_rule[].default_scrolling_extent.desc: Initial fractional extent along the strip.

window_rule[].default_scrolling_extent_p.desc: Initial logical-pixel extent along the strip.

window_rule[].default_workspace.desc: Open on a one-based position or exact workspace name.

window_rule[].focus_on_activate.desc: Override activation focus for this window.

window_rule[].hdr.desc: Override the focused output's HDR policy.

window_rule[].match.app_id.desc: Match the application ID with a regular expression.

window_rule[].match.at_startup.desc: Match during or after the first 60 seconds.

window_rule[].match.is_alone.desc: Match whether this is the only tiled window.

window_rule[].match.is_only_window.desc: Match whether this is the only window on its workspace, floating ones included.

window_rule[].match.xdg_tag.desc: Match a client-defined XDG toplevel tag.

window_rule[].vrr.desc: Override the focused output's VRR policy.

window_rule[].window_effect.desc: Replace `effects.window` with a window preset or pool, or `"off"` to disable it.

workspace[].index.desc: Select a current one-based position from 1 to 64.

workspace[].layout.client_maximize.desc: Choose `"column"` or `"edges"` for a tiled window's own maximize request; see Maximize and fullscreen.

workspace[].layout.dwindle.new_toward_cu.desc: Open new windows on the pointer's side of the split.

workspace[].layout.master.new_becomes_ma.desc: Give the master slot to new windows.

workspace[].layout.master.new_on_top.desc: Place new stack windows at the top or bottom.

workspace[].layout.master.position.desc: Place the master area left, right, or center.

workspace[].layout.new_exits_fullscreen.desc: Choose which arriving windows exit fullscreen; see Leaving fullscreen.

workspace[].layout.scrolling.center_focu.desc: Control when focus changes center a column.

workspace[].layout.scrolling.center_unde.desc: Center or start-align an underfull strip.

workspace[].name.desc: Select an exact name and create it on matching dynamic outputs.

workspace[].output.desc: Restrict the rule to a connector or monitor name.

workspaces.back_and_forth.desc: Selecting the active workspace returns to the previous one on that output.

workspaces.empty_above.desc: Keep a leading empty workspace on dynamic outputs.

actions.intro: Actions are the compositor's verbs. Bind one under `[keybinds]`, attach it to a hot corner, or run it with `umbriel msg <action>`. `umbriel msg --help` prints this same list, with the same wording and the same grouping. See Keybinds for chord syntax and IPC for the socket behind `umbriel msg`, including the event stream that reports what an action changed.
actions.title: Actions

animation.intro: Animation settings live under `[animation]`. The top-level values provide defaults, and each event can override them.
animation.title: Animation

appearance.intro: Configure Umbriel's colors, window decorations, blur, and shadows.
appearance.title: Appearance

configuration.intro: The packaged starting configuration is `examples/config.toml`. Copy it before making local changes:
configuration.title: Configuration

effects.intro: Effects are GLSL programs Umbriel runs on animation events, on the focused window's border, on windows, on whole outputs, and around the pointer. Every effect is off until you select one. Umbriel ships a small set; each is a preset you include and then name where it should apply.
effects.title: Effects

index.intro: Umbriel is a Wayland compositor with scrolling and tiling layouts, independent workspaces per monitor, and configurable visual effects. It works on its own or with Noctalia, a desktop shell designed to integrate with Umbriel.
index.title: Umbriel

input.intro: Configure keyboard, pointer, touchpad, tablet, cursor, and focus behavior under `[input]`.
input.title: Input

installation.intro: Umbriel is packaged for several Linux distributions. Prefer a distribution package when one is available; it provides the simplest installation and upgrade path.
installation.title: Installing Umbriel

ipc.intro: Umbriel exposes a local UNIX socket for queries, actions, and event subscriptions. Most users should use the `umbriel` command rather than connect to the socket directly.
ipc.title: IPC

keybinds.intro: Configure bindings under `[keybinds]`. See Actions for the complete action list.
keybinds.title: Keybinds

layer-rules.intro: Layer rules apply visual effects to layer-shell surfaces such as bars, launchers, and notifications. Run `umbriel layers` to list active namespaces.
layer-rules.title: Layer Rules

layout.intro: Choose one layout mode for each workspace. Configure the default globally, then use workspace rules for exceptions.
layout.title: Layout

outputs.intro: Output sections configure monitors by connector name, such as `DP-1`, or by monitor identity:
outputs.title: Outputs

scratchpad.intro: A scratchpad stores windows outside normal workspaces so they can be shown or hidden quickly. Its windows float and appear together.
scratchpad.title: Scratchpads

security.intro: Umbriel keeps the current desktop visible while an `ext-session-lock-v1` client prepares a mapped lock surface for every active output. The client has up to three seconds to provide those surfaces. Umbriel then switches every output to the lock scene and reports the session as locked only after each active output has presented a secure frame.
security.title: Security

streaming.intro: Sunshine streams a desktop to Moonlight clients. Pointed at a virtual output, it streams a monitor that exists only for the session, at the client's resolution and frame rate, while the physical monitors keep their layout.
streaming.title: Game streaming

window-rules.intro: Window rules apply settings to matching applications. Every matching rule contributes its values; when two set the same field, the later rule wins.
window-rules.title: Window Rules

workspaces.intro: Each output has its own workspaces. Choose a dynamic or fixed model, then use workspace rules to customize individual entries.
workspaces.title: Workspaces

workspaces-overview.intro: The overview displays every workspace and lets you navigate, focus, close, and move windows.
workspaces-overview.title: Workspaces Overview

tables.<output>: Connector or monitor name. Bare `dpms-off` and `dpms-on` target every configured output
tables.<scratchpad>: Scratchpad name. The bare form selects the implicit `default` scratchpad, which exists only when no named scratchpads are configured
tables.<window-id>: The same id; the bare action targets the focused window
tables.animation.overview: Overview opening, closing, and filmstrip movement
tables.animation.windows_move: Position during moves, reflow, maximize, and restore
tables.skip-confirmation: `session-quit` only: quit without the on-screen confirmation
